en: Adding tasks to the project works the same
way we saw it before in our session. So the
general interface doesn't change.
You have your text area where you can add
the task to Claude. Down here, you can see
the folder that is used for this specific
project.
Next, you have an Ask button, which allows
you to select if Claude pauses so you can
approve each action,
or if you want Claude to simply work without
pausing for approval. I always keep the
approval step on to make sure nothing
unintended is happening.
Now, before we start our tasks though, we'll
have a look at the right sidebar here.
At the top, we can find our instructions. We
saw these before when we created the
project. In here, you can also edit those.
So in case something additional is provided
to the project, in case you want to update
anything, you can always work on these
instructions. And you can also show the
entire instructions here with the Show More
option.
The scheduled part is something we'll skip
so far. We'll have a look at this after we
had a look at the projects.
The context though down here is very
interesting.
As mentioned, you can find the memory at the
bottom.
So we can ask Claude to remember something
and it will save it here. So it will update
its knowledge about us, about the project.
And we also have
the upper context section which has this on
your computer menu which contains the Spring
Meeting details we saw in our folder that we
used at the beginning when creating the
project. But it also contains these 2
additional files that we added, the assigned
contact and the call transcript. These files
are now copied into that project. So as
mentioned, we can't just skip that
copy-pasting part to our folder. We can just
add any files we need when creating the
project. There are more context options now
though, after the project is created.
With the plus symbol, we can either add a
link. As ACME is not a real company here, I
could just add
our Academind website here as a link, which
will then be used as context in this
project, which won't be too helpful here, so
I'll get rid of this.
And the second option is to choose a folder.
Now you might ask, why would I again want to
add more context to my project? If we think
about this campaign here, we have ACME as a
company and we are working in the Spring
Meeting project now.
But ACME could have some general information
that might be relevant for this project,
which I don't necessarily want to add to
this project folder though.
One example could be branding guidelines,
color guidelines about ACME, what their
corporate identity looks like, their CI, et
cetera. So things that are important for the
company in general but not related to this
specific project. Now, for such examples,
you can simply choose the corresponding
folder.
Here, this is the Brand Assets folder, which
contains the colors, the logo rules, and the
typography.
And by adding this, Claude will have access
to this folder but not copy that content
into our current project folder. So it moves
out of the project folder, out of the
project workspace, and adds additional
information as context here. As we now added
these brand assets, we can of course also
update our instructions accordingly. So we
can add something like, when working with
brand assets, check the shared brand assets
folder I've added as context. This instructs
Claude specifically to also check that
information if you're working on anything
like that.
With this, we also edited our instructions
and we now fully understood all the context
and all the information we can bring into
this project. Now it's time to start our
tasks, to start working on the project.
